analysis: Pilot M risk-set design hardening and common-support diagnostic
canonical_claim_boundary: Mechanism pilot only; not prospective prevalence or predictive performance.

design_corrections.provisional_robust_candidates: recorded but excluded from the primary risk-set case set until cross-source trajectory/B validation

interpretation: OpenAlex sample=N is not nested as N changes, so v3/v4 reservoir-size comparisons were confounded by control-pool replacement.
Deterministic multi-seed acquisition creates nested support sets larger than the one-page 100-work API limit.
Standard incidence-density reuse across distinct risk sets improves the 1:1 all-robust diagnostic but does not solve balance.
Increasing to four controls per case worsens balance because weakly comparable additional controls are forced into sparse historical risk sets.
The fixed literature-known case analysis still fails the abs-SMD < 0.10 gate.
Washburn 1921 shows the clearest common-support shortage in the acquired reservoir.
next_gate: Enumerate the complete same-field same-publication-year OpenAlex frame for the three known cases rather than draw another random reservoir.
Reconstruct only the full-frame candidates needed for event-time eligibility and rerun frozen 1:1 support diagnostics without relaxing abs-SMD < 0.10.
If complete-frame overlap still fails, freeze an overlap-limited estimand / unmatched-case rule before any mechanism inference rather than force a match.
Independently validate OpenAlex annual citation trajectory / Beauty Coefficient against SciSciNet-v2 or another bibliographic source.
